output.summary: The yield fall is real: gauge R&R, CMM program and criteria are unchanged, and customer PPM rose. New operators are cleared: they reject at the same rate as experienced operators, and the decline began before they ran alone. Three candidate causes are confounded and cannot yet be separated: Corvane bar hardness spread, worn spindles after the deferred service, and 12-hour fatigue. Corvane ran only after Aug 3 and the spindles were never serviced on it. Scrap-tag timing is an artifact, so it says nothing about fatigue. Spindle deferral was driven by backlog pressure. Reverting shifts, cancelling the contract, punishing operators or cutting inspection are unjustified. Staggered service with Tamsworth trials and hour-of-machining matching is the best step.
